specs.scene: A documentary photograph inside a small trade shop, an old corded telephone ringing unanswered on a cluttered service counter, its cord looped over a stack of invoices, the background counter surfaces left blank and out of focus, natural window light falling across the phone as the single sharp element in the frame.
specs.source_quote: 85 percent of callers who hit voicemail never call back

recognisable.why: A ringing telephone on a trade counter reads instantly without explanation, though it is a generic object rather than a branded one.

legibility.why: One focal mass, the ringing phone, with everything else deliberately blank.

curiosity.why: The caption states a flat verdict about behavior the viewer cannot see resolved in the frame, inviting the 'why' without answering it.

subject.why: The phone functions as a single distinctive object anchor even in a documentary-style frame.

credible.why: No figure is carried at all, which the rubric scores as full.

stakes.why: Implies a permanent, not just delayed, loss of business to the viewer.

reexpress.why: Gives the consequence of the missed call rather than restating any of the titles' own missed-call statistic.

specs.scene: A single unbranded office answering machine sits alone on an empty countertop, its message light lit, phone cord trailing off the edge of the frame, the surface behind it left plainly blank and evenly lit so the machine is the only thing the eye has to resolve.
specs.source_quote: a plumber missing 15 calls a week at $350 a job

recognisable.why: An answering machine is an everyday physical object anyone recognises instantly, even unbranded.

legibility.why: One object fills the frame with no competing elements.

curiosity.why: The figure resolves the point on sight, leaving little the viewer needs to keep looking for.

subject.why: A single distinctive object anchor, exactly as the archetype requires.

credible.why: The weekly figure is derived from a stated per-job rate and call count, a believable, smallest honest unit.

stakes.why: States a direct, ongoing dollar loss to the viewer's own business.

reexpress.why: Trades the titles' percentage framing for a concrete weekly dollar loss, a different and more visceral unit.

specs.scene: A technician crouches on a rooftop mid-repair, wrench in hand, tool belt visible, one clean half of the frame left as open sky, the work surface and tools sharply in focus while the sky behind remains a flat, blank plane for the overlay.
specs.source_quote: The technician is on a roof, the dentist is with a patient

recognisable.why: A tradesperson mid-repair on a roof is instantly legible as an everyday trade with no explanation needed.

legibility.why: One person performing one action fills the frame.

curiosity.why: The caption states the obvious visible fact rather than an unresolved judgement.

subject.why: A person mid-action is a textbook single anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried, scoring full by the rubric's own rule.

stakes.why: Implies lost business only implicitly, through the visual absence of a phone in hand.

reexpress.why: Shares the missed-call subject with the titles but adds little beyond restating the premise in image form.

specs.scene: Inside a small florist shop on a peak delivery day, a corded phone rings on a counter buried under wrapped bouquets, the surrounding buckets and blank order slips rendered soft and out of focus so the ringing phone remains the one sharp point in an otherwise busy, blank-surfaced room.
specs.source_quote: the florist is buried on Valentine's Day

recognisable.why: A florist shop is an immediately recognisable everyday trade setting.

legibility.why: The busy environment risks reading as several separate elements even with the phone favored, short of a single clean mass.

curiosity.why: The caption names what the image already shows plainly, leaving little unresolved.

subject.why: The environment itself is the argument, which weakens the single clear anchor the rubric asks for.

credible.why: No figure is carried, scoring full by the rubric's own rule.

stakes.why: Implies lost orders during a peak period, a real but only implied threat.

reexpress.why: Largely restates the visible scene rather than adding a consequence the title does not already carry.
